1. Scope

This list reflects components actually linked and used by the current kikitalk iOS target, rather than all dependencies of other sample projects in the repository. Communication components are enabled for selected features after you agree to the applicable Privacy Policy; system permissions are requested in the relevant scenario. Third-party processing must follow agreed purposes and applicable law. Send personal information requests to operator Li Hao (李浩) at 2114581274@qq.com.

2. LiveKit Swift SDK

Component: LiveKit Swift Client SDK 2.18.0, published as open source by LiveKit. Purpose: connect to self-hosted voice chat nodes when users enter rooms and actively turn on their microphones, publish, subscribe to and play live audio, and handle connection status and room data notifications. Our service interfaces manage account authorization, mic seats, text content and announcement permissions.

Necessary processing includes public user and room identifiers, live audio you actively publish, device and system versions, network connections and communication quality. The current configuration connects to self-hosted signaling and media nodes at https://furby.top/; LiveKit Cloud room services are not configured. Recording, transcription and AI voice services are not integrated. Official source: https://github.com/livekit/client-sdk-swift. Self-hosting documentation: https://docs.livekit.io/transport/self-hosting/.

3. Bundled WebRTC and native dependencies

Pinned dependencies currently include LiveKitWebRTC 150.7871.3 and LiveKitUniFFI 0.1.9, distributed with LiveKit to provide necessary native real-time communication and bridging. They are not separate advertising, payment or commercial analytics services. Audio encoding, decoding and network adaptation do not mean the app has enabled recording storage. Network and diagnostic processing is limited to what is necessary for the selected communication feature.

4. Apple system sign-in and identity services

Components: the iOS AuthenticationServices framework and Sign in with Apple. Provider: Apple. Purpose: account authorization initiated by the user, server verification, status checks and revocation on account deletion. The system framework comes with iOS; no separate third-party sign-in SDK is embedded.

Necessary processing: the developer-scoped user identifier provided by Apple, identity token, one-time authorization code, random challenge and tokens used to manage authorization. This version does not actively request or store Apple names or emails or submit Apple passwords to our service server. Authentication requests access Apple services and are handled under its rules. Official information: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/zh-cn/sign-in-with-apple/.

5. Apple system notifications and APNs

Components: iOS UserNotifications, UIApplication remote-notification registration and Apple Push Notification service (APNs). Provider: Apple. Purpose: after active user authorization, send private-message and interaction alerts and necessary badges to signed-in devices, and handle notification taps. No additional third-party push SDK is included.

Necessary processing: the device push token Apple provides for this app, app identifier, notification payload and random event identifier. Default payloads may include the sender’s current nickname, private message text or in-app interaction summaries. You can enable “Hide Message Content” in the app’s notification settings so later alerts use generic wording without text or nicknames. Pushes contain no photos, image content or room names. The account service manages a random installation identifier associated with a valid session. Push private keys remain only on restricted servers. Apple Privacy Policy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/zh-cn/.

6. System components and features outside the enabled scope

Interfaces, networking, photo selection, audio devices and secure storage use iOS system components such as SwiftUI, UIKit, URLSession, PhotosUI, AVAudioSession and Keychain. Photo avatars load from the account service at kiki.group and are cached locally; preset avatars are included in the app.

The current production kikitalk target no longer links Tencent voice chat, live broadcasting, Room Engine or IM SDKs. It does not use separate advertising analytics, payment, content moderation, AI transcription or vendor push SDKs. Tencent reference projects retained in the repository are outside this target. This list will be updated if third-party processing is added or its purpose changes.
